subtopics.title: Molecular Motion — the Kinetic Model of a Gas

questions.question: The kinetic model explains gas pressure as:
options: The weight of the gas pressing down
Attractions between molecules and the walls
The combined effect of countless molecular collisions with the container walls

questions.question: The absolute temperature of a gas is directly proportional to the molecules':
Heating a gas affects the speeds of its molecules by:
options: Giving every molecule the same higher speed
Speeding up only the slowest molecules
Shifting the whole distribution of speeds toward higher values

questions.question: A temperature of 30 °C expressed in kelvin is:
The two idealisations of an ideal gas are that its particles:
options: Have negligible volume and exert no forces between collisions

questions.question: Real gases behave MOST ideally at:
At low temperature the ideal model fails because:
options: Collisions become too fast to count
Slow-moving molecules give the weak attractive forces time to act

questions.question: The real gases closest to ideal behaviour are:

Gas at 80 kPa occupies 3 dm³. Compressed to 0,75 dm³ at constant temperature, its pressure becomes:
Plotting p against 1/V for Boyle's law data gives:
options: A straight line through the origin — the proof of inverse proportionality

subtopics.title: A Room Full of Super Balls

questions.question: In the super-ball picture, pressure is:
options: The relentless drizzle of tiny molecular knocks on the walls
One large shove from the whole gas
The weight of the balls collecting on the floor
The balls sticking to the walls

questions.question: Absolute zero, at −273 °C, is the temperature where:
The ideal gas is called a "nearly-true pretence" because the model:
options: Pretends molecules are sizeless and never attract each other — nearly true when far apart and fast

subtopics.title: Squeeze the Bottle — Boyle in Your Hands

questions.question: Crushing a capped bottle to half its volume doubles the pressure because:
options: Each molecule reaches a wall twice as often, doubling the collision rate

questions.question: The one-sentence version of Boyle's law is:
options: Pressure divided by volume never changes

questions.question: At 80 kPa a gas fills 3 dm³. Squeezed to 0,75 dm³ at the same temperature, the pressure must become:
A bicycle pump resists hardest near the end of the stroke because:
options: The pump runs out of oil
The trapped air's pressure has climbed as its volume shrank

questions.question: A capped bottle in a hot parked car goes drum-tight because:
options: The heat quickens the molecules, and quicker molecules knock harder on the walls
Air leaks in through the cap
The plastic shrinks in the heat
The water inside expands into gas

questions.question: 40 °C is not "twice as hot" as 20 °C because measured from absolute zero the temperatures are:
options: 313 K and 293 K — nearly the same

questions.question: The universal gas constant R equals:
pV = nRT lets you "take a census of invisible molecules" because:
options: Measuring pressure, volume and temperature reveals n, the number of moles
